One `/mcp` endpoint now serves both legacy stateful sessions (`Mcp-Session-Id`) and session-less per-request-negotiated POSTs (protocol 2026-07-28) via rmcp 3.5.1 — ChatGPT-style connectors and Claude-style stateful clients share a single URL.

## Changes

- **rmcp 1.7 → 3.5.1** (#275): the Streamable HTTP transport serves legacy sessions and session-less per-request clients concurrently on the same endpoint (`legacy_session_mode`). The vendored rmcp 0.1.5 legacy SSE transport (`--sse-port`) is unchanged.
- **MCP tasks move to SEP-2663** (`io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks`), replacing the removed SEP-1319 utility: clients that declare the extension run `run_js` as a task (`tasks/get` / `tasks/cancel`, result inline on completion, 300s retention); clients that don't keep synchronous results. Task state is shared across service instances so session-less clients can poll from later requests.
- **Auth**: bearer-token enforcement (`--jwks-url`) verified fail-closed for session-less requests, with new e2e coverage; request-header values (Authorization/Cookie) no longer reach logs at any level.
- **Tooling**: new `cut-release` workflow (#276, #277) for one-step releases.

## Validation

255/255 lib unit tests; MCP transport suites green including the rewritten SEP-2663 `tasks_e2e` and new `sessionless_http_e2e` / `jwks_auth_e2e`. Verified live: a single session-less POST executes `run_js` with no initialize and no session id, a legacy session works concurrently on the same endpoint, and a session-less task is pollable across requests.

Known-red: `pi-harness-e2e` fails building the external `pi` checkout (pre-existing, unrelated to this release).
